lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice comparatives for everyday preferences and weather talk.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Colleagues compare days, weather, coffee, or lunch options during fika.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik compare today's weather, coffee, and lunch options and say which one is better or warmer.

main_focus.name: comparatives with än
main_focus.description: Use comparative adjective forms plus än to compare two everyday things.
model_examples: Det är varmare idag än igår.
Det här kaffet är godare än det gamla.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use comparative forms naturally 4-6 times in the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.theme: comparisons of weather, days, and food
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use practical comparative chunks rather than abstract adjective lists.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker comments on the weather, coffee, or lunch.
dialogue_shape.middle: They compare two options and give simple reactions.
dialogue_shape.ending: They end with agreement or a light preference.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat comparatives with concrete nouns and clear comparisons

focus: which option is preferred and why
the final shared opinion or disagreement

sentence_focus: one sentence with warmer or colder weather
one sentence comparing coffee or food
one question asking for a preference
one sentence agreeing or disagreeing simply
